newsitem.title: JAPAN: CSCE president says white sugar futures will grow.
newsitem.headline: CSCE president says white sugar futures will grow.

text.p: The New York Coffee, Sugar & Cocoa Exchange's (CSCE) white sugar futures contract launched last June will gain more business, the exchange's president said on Tuesday.
But Japanese traders remained sceptical about the contract.
"We'll draw more people to trade because we're the best place to hedge. The market will improve natural liquidity," CSCE president James Bowe said in a speech to the Tokyo Grain Exchange.

Although he said trading volume in CSCE white sugar futures was less than expected, he cited increasing white sugar exports from India as a factor that would help draw attention to the new contract as a hedging tool.
The CSCE contract offered advantages to London's white sugar futures contract, including the use of polypropylene bags instead of jute.
But Japanese traders saw little likelihood that they would use the contract to a significant degree. They already used the London contract and Japan imported very little white sugar.

"We're active users of the CSCE's raw sugar futures. But given Japan's low level of white sugar imports, we can't find any strong reason to trade the white sugar contract, except for pure speculation," a senior official of a major trade house said.

While Japan's raw sugar imports in January-November 1996 totalled about 1.52 million tonnes, white sugar imports, which are assessed a duty of 50 yen per kg, were only 2,300 tonnes, Finance Ministry data showed.
